contentGapNotes: Article does not explain *why* Webflow chose the 'agentic' category name or whether it stuck in the market—only that it was deployed. Searchers may want to know if category naming worked as a competitive moat.

No mention of traffic or conversion impact from these changes—article correctly avoids claiming outcomes, but searchers may want guidance on how to measure whether similar changes move their own metrics.

Missing analysis of whether Webflow's removal of social proof CTAs ('Dell prototypes faster') correlates with brand recognition milestones or customer acquisition cost trends—context that would help readers assess whether *their* brand is ready for the same move.

No discussion of how SEO strategy may have shifted alongside homepage messaging (e.g., keyword targeting, organic search positioning). The article focuses on CRO and messaging but ignores whether homepage changes aimed at organic ranking improvements.
Limited guidance on testing methodology—article suggests 'founder tests' but does not address A/B testing duration, statistical significance, or sample size needed to validate these messaging shifts.
No comparison to competitors' homepage evolution (Framer, Webstudio, etc.) to contextualize whether Webflow's upmarket shift was defensive or offensive positioning.
requiredFixes: The primary keyword 'Webflow homepage CRO teardown' appears in the title but is not naturally woven into the body text in the first 200 words—add one natural mention of this phrase in the intro or 'Quick answer' section to strengthen on-page keyword relevance.

Meta description claims the article covers 'headline, section headings, CTAs, navigation' but the article focuses heavily on headline and CTA with lighter coverage of section headings and navigation changes. Either expand the navigation analysis or adjust the meta description to match content.
